Do you have stiffness mainly in your neck and trunk rather than your limbs?
Have you or your family noticed changes in your personality, judgment, or motivation?
Do you have slurred speech or difficulty swallowing?
Do you have a resting tremor in your hands?
Do you feel lightheaded or dizzy when you stand up?

results: 1. MRI brain with thin-section sagittal views through the midbrain to assess for the hummingbird sign and MR Parkinsonism Index
brain MRI: no structural lesion accounting for the syndrome
2. Cardiac MIBG scintigraphy to assess cardiac sympathetic denervation
3. DaTscan (dopamine transporter SPECT) to confirm presynaptic dopaminergic deficit

video-oculography / eye-movement recording: vertical gaze palsy progressing to complete external ophthalmoplegia

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Progressive supranuclear palsy, Richardson syndrome — a sporadic 4R-tau neurodegenerative disorder

1. Niemann-Pick type C disease (vertical supranuclear gaze palsy, early onset, rapid progression; plasma cholestane-3β,5α,6β-triol and lyso-sphingomyelin-509 could not be performed)
2. Multiple system atrophy, parkinsonian subtype (would expect autonomic failure and ataxia, but gaze palsy is uncommon)
3. Corticobasal degeneration (typically asymmetric apraxia, cortical sensory loss, alien limb — none present here, but early-onset levodopa-unresponsive tauopathy remains possible)
